block.title: CPU startup proofs export their checked specifications
block.p: Glibc’s CPU startup proofs now state the contracts that their callers need. The full proofs infer a plan for each call, check its invariants, and prove that its result equals the stated contract. Rocq can build a proof interface without running that inference.

On swa, with dependencies already compiled, a rocq c -vos run for CpuCache fell from 43.5 seconds to 0.9 seconds. CpuInit fell from 19.4 seconds to 1.0 second. CpuHello now gets object addresses from the loader’s placement tables. Its interface took 0.9 seconds against 12.3 seconds before the change.
